plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Plant Tropisms, Auxin & Ethylene Hormone chart from Charles & Francis Darwin (November 1880 The Power of Movement in Plants), Gottlieb Haberlandt & Bohumil Němec (1900 Ber. Dtsch. Bot. Ges.), Peter Boysen-Jensen (1910–1913), Frits Warmolt Went (1926/1928 Proc. K. Akad. Wet. Amsterdam 30: 10–19), and Dmitry Neljubow (1901) & Richard Gane (1934 Nature 134: 1008) shows 1) Phototropism: blue light on the 1–2 mm coleoptile tip redistributes auxin (indole-3-acetic acid) to the shaded side, elongating shaded stem cells; 2) Gravitropism: falling amyloplast statoliths in root-cap cells redirect auxin to the lower side, inhibiting lower root cells so the root bends down; and 3) Ethylene (C2H4) gas triggering fruit ripening.

teach_overlay.detail: Inked Darwin (1880) & Frits Went (17 April 1926) coleoptile phototropism & agar-block curvature bioassay chart (uncovered tip bends toward light; tin-foil-capped tip = 0° bend; asymmetric auxin agar block in darkness = curvature proportional to auxin concentration) on period paper
teach_overlay.scale: a plant doesn't bend toward a window by flexing muscles on the sunny side — it pumps auxin growth hormone to the shady side so the shady cells inflate with water and stretch longer like the outer rail of a curving train track
